content:
sam: Heads up — onboarding Kaleido-7B (fp16 -> int8) looks mostly fine perf-wise but we see a consistent Rouge-L drop (~3.2) on summarization suite vs fp16. Suspect rotary / tokenizer normalization interaction. :thinking:
anya: can you paste the exact eval diff and the conversion command you used?
ravi: +1, also which quant backend (awq/q4/q8) and per-channel/per-tensor?
sam: Eval snippet: `avg_rouge_l: fp16=42.7, int8=39.5`; command: `python convert.py --model kaleido-7b --to int8 --backend awq --per-channel`
modelbench-bot: CI: modelbench/kaleido7b-int8 — 3 failed tests, 12 passed — see /ci/artifacts/5955551234/logs
anya: hmm. Was tokenizer normalization run? Kaleido uses legacy unicode NFKC folding in its vocab; our tokenizer pipeline auto-normalizes to NFD in the hosted conversion, so token ids shift for combined diacritics. Could be prompt split differences causing prefix KV mismatch.
sam: we used `--use-host-tokenizer` flag. I also ran a local quick check: matched token ids for short inputs but long-context diffs appear.
ravi: that smells like KV-cache misalignment when rotary params are applied per-head vs shared. If conversion flipped head-order, rotary phase will be applied to wrong dims.
luis: quick sanity: upload the converted model metadata (config.json) from the artifact and the original. I can diff head dims and rotary params.
sam: pasted configs to /ci/artifacts/5955551234/configs (links in thread). snippet of converted config: ```json
{"n_heads": 32, "rotary_emb": true, "rotary_base": 10000, "head_dim": 64, "head_mapping": "interleaved"}
```
anya: and original config?
sam: original: ```json
{"n_heads": 32, "rotary_emb": true, "rotary_base": 8192, "head_dim": 64, "head_mapping": "standard"}
```
ravi: bingo. rotary_base changed from 8192 -> 10000 during conversion. That will change rotary angle scaling and easily cause generation drift. Why did converter pick 10000? that's the default for some export libs.
anya: also head_mapping mismatch — converter set interleaved ordering while original is standard. That changes how KV cache is packed and how per-head scales are applied.
sam: I didn't notice that. Conversion script excerpt: ```bash
python convert.py --model kaleido-7b --set-rotary-base 10000 --reorder-heads interleave
``` I must have run a preset.
luis: proposal: re-run conversion with `--preserve-rotary-base` and `--preserve-head-order`, then quantize. Also run a small compare: generate logits for first 256 tokens on a deterministic prompt and diff L2 between fp16 logits and int8 logits.
ravi: add test for tokenization parity across long inputs: run tokenizer on >2048 tokens with both host tokenizer and model tokenizer to ensure no invisible normalization differences. Script: ```python
# quick parity check
from tokenizer import Tokenizer
t1 = Tokenizer('host')
t2 = Tokenizer('model')
for msg in long_inputs:
    assert t1.encode(msg)==t2.encode(msg)
```
anya: extra: check quant backing implementation: awq defaults to per-channel scales but can quantize rotary weights differently. There was an AWQ bug that applied asymmetric scaling to rotary projection matrices once, which skewed angles.
sam: re-run queued with flags: `--preserve-rotary-base --preserve-head-order --tokenizer=embedded --backend=awq --per-channel --rotary-exact` — kicking off now. :rocket: Will post results.
modelbench-bot: Job queued: modelbench/kaleido7b-int8-rerun (#5955551234-rerun) started.
luis: if rerun doesn't recover, we should test int4 and q4f16 as sanity — sometimes int4 has different rounding that by chance preserves steady rotary scaling.
ravi: also remember to run a few examples with forced sampling seeds to inspect qualitative diffs — sometimes Rouge misses fluency regressions.
anya: thanks — also add a small unit to our conversion tests that verifies `rotary_base` and `head_mapping` preserved after conversion. It'll catch this very quickly next time. :thumbsup:
sam: agreed, filing a small PR to add those asserts to the conversion e2e tests after rerun. Will update thread with numbers.
modelbench-bot: Job completed: modelbench/kaleido7b-int8-rerun — 0 failed, 15 passed — rerun artifacts at /ci/artifacts/5955551299/results
sam: rerun result: Rouge-L fp16=42.7, int8-rerun=42.5 — regression mostly closed. So root cause = rotary_base + head-order mismatch + tokenization preset. Thanks all. :tada:
